A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonMed work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated experiments and retained output examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality evaluations, medical QA fine-tuning results, training-duration comparisons, and analyses of model complementarity.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports a 14B model result, physician-review findings, and a quantitative decoding-temperature sweep.

M1.justification: The generator models, six-step reasoning template, difficulty routing, component prompts, and CoT/Response/Reason training formulations are retained. Added descriptions of localized refinement and self-consistency do not establish a changed implementation. The 14B experiment applies the existing training approach; reinforcement learning is discussed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same medical data sources and evaluation coverage: MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and six medical MMLU subjects. The physician review, larger backbone, and decoding sweep do not introduce a documented new medical task, domain, or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds direct GPT-o1 distillation of all items as a cost comparator against selective EMD processing in Table 8. Dataset-quality comparators and predictive-performance baselines remain unchanged, including the larger models in v1 Table 7, retained as v2 Table 11.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation of a 14B backbone, physician review of 100 randomly sampled cases, and an eleven-temperature sweep from 0.0 to 1.0 with other parameters fixed. These substantially extend the experimental design. Existing benchmark splits and sample counts remain unchanged; the newly listed training hyperparameters are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses examine physician-assessed reasoning quality, systematic sensitivity to decoding temperature, scaling beyond 7B, and the cost benefit of selective GPT-o1 use. The original refinement ablation, reasoning-granularity and epoch comparisons, model-complementarity analyses, and illustrative outputs are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly identifies the retained illustrative outputs as single-run, non-cherry-picked examples. Existing benchmark uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and the temperature table follows the same plus/minus format. No new repeated-seed study, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Original result values are retained. New results include ReasonMed-14B's prose-reported 72.8% overall accuracy, temperature-sweep totals of 69.1% for greedy decoding versus 69.4% at temperatures 0.5–0.7, and physician-review percentages of 87%, 82%, 68%, and 35%. Table 8 also adds reported costs of $16,631 versus $4,552.47. No per-benchmark ReasonMed-14B results are tabulated.

T1.justification: The data-representation mappings in Section 4.1 are substantively unchanged. Neither version develops theorems or proofs, and the added empirical and cost analyses introduce no substantive formal theory.

C1.justification: v2 retains the dataset and hybrid-reasoning contributions but expands its central claims to competitive 14B scaling and cost-efficient curation. It also strengthens the contribution framing from a systematic evaluation of explicit reasoning to a controlled study isolating reasoning from dense knowledge injection.

C2.justification: The scalability limitation moves from models above 7B to models above 14B, while LLM-judge bias remains a concern despite physician review. v2 adds interpretations of localized error correction, moderate-temperature decoding, clinical citation/specificity gaps, and output variability. The research-only applicability boundary remains.

D1.justification: New Appendices C–D disclose the learning-rate schedule, warmup, batch/accumulation settings, context length, precision, DeepSpeed configuration, and default decoding parameters. Compute and cost tables add generation time, serving hardware, GPU-hours, and token pricing. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The direct model-access link present on v1's first page is removed, without establishing that the model itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds an explicit comparison of its dataset focus with Lingshu's multimodal modeling focus, introduces citations including FineReason, RAPID, MR-BEN, and LLaMA-Factory, and removes Storm-born. The broader positioning around multi-agent curation, medical reasoning, and LLM evaluation remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Component explanations expand, and four new appendix sections precede the relocated original appendices. Editing also introduces a duplicated paragraph in Section 3.2 and an unresolved 'Section ??' reference in Section 4.1.

P2.justification: New Tables 5–8 substantially expand the displays to cover compute, hyperparameters, temperature sensitivity, and cost. Existing figures retain their content but move within the document, and appendix material is reflowed. v2 also duplicates the larger-model baseline display as Tables 11 and 12; this duplication supplies no additional results.

improvement.justification: The newly disclosed optimization and decoding settings, together with the systematic temperature sweep, make the retained approach easier to reproduce and assess. Scaling and physician-review additions partially address v1's limitations, but reporting remains sparse: 14B results lack a benchmark breakdown and physician-review procedures are unspecified. New cost arithmetic inconsistencies and duplicated tables further limit the gains. The clearest net benefit is improved technical transparency.
